T: Last day of school. Nobody's going home.
D: On the last day of school in 1976, Texas teens party at the moon tower.
P: Serve the snacks when everyone gathers at the Moon Tower party.
S: Pool hall nuts, mind the paint on O'Bannion

Salted peanuts and pretzel twists roasted in chilli butter, smoked paprika and a little brown sugar until glossy and crunchy, served warm in paper cups. Melt 50g butter with 1 tsp chilli flakes, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tbsp brown sugar and 2 tsp Worcestershire sauce. Toss with 250g salted roasted peanuts and 150g pretzel twists on a lined tray. Bake at 160C for 15 minutes, stirring once halfway, until the coating is dry and glossy. Cool for 10 minutes so they crisp up, then tip into paper cups.
Onion chive dip and thick chips. Slater climbs the tower.
Thick-cut chips with French onion dip: onions caramelised slowly for 40 minutes, cooled, folded into sour cream with salt and chives.
Pretzel rods dipped in peanut butter, then milk chocolate
Pretzel rods dipped in smooth peanut butter warmed with a little honey, then half-dipped in melted milk chocolate, set on baking paper.
M: Texas salt and pepper brisket with pickles
Brisket after mailbox baseball. Mind the gun.

Brisket rubbed with coarse salt and cracked pepper, roasted low for ten hours until it wobbles, sliced thick on white bread with pickles, onion and barbecue sauce. Rub a 2.5kg beef brisket with 2 tbsp coarse salt and 2 tbsp cracked black pepper and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight. Roast fat side up on a rack at 120C for 9 to 10 hours until the thickest part reaches 95C. Wrap in foil and baking paper and rest 1 hour. Slice thick against the grain and serve on soft white bread with sliced dill pickles, thin raw onion and 250ml smoky barbecue sauce.
Breaded minute steak shallow fried, with peppery cream gravy
Thin beef steaks dipped in seasoned flour and egg, shallow fried Texas style and smothered in peppery cream gravy.
W: Last day of '76 sweet tea ice blocks
Black tea sweetened with sugar and lemon, frozen on sticks

Strong black tea sweetened while hot, lemon juice stirred in, cooled and frozen in moulds with sticks for at least 6 hours. Steep 4 black tea bags in 750ml boiling water for 5 minutes. Stir in 100g sugar while hot, add the juice of a lemon and cool. Pour into ice block moulds, add sticks and freeze at least 6 hours.
K: Cold lager with lime, tomato juice and hot sauce, chilli salt rim

Ice-cold lager poured over lime, tomato juice, hot sauce and Worcestershire in a chilli salt rimmed glass, a lime wedge on the side. Mix 1 tbsp salt with 1 tsp chilli powder on a saucer. Rub the rims of 4 pint glasses with a lime wedge and dip in the salt. Fill with ice. Add to each glass 30ml lime juice, 60ml tomato juice, 3 dashes hot sauce and 2 dashes Worcestershire sauce. Top each slowly with 330ml cold lager, stir once and serve with a lime wedge.

s.note: Onion chive dip and thick chips. Slater climbs the tower.
s.how: Cook 2 sliced onions slowly in a little oil for 40 minutes until deep brown, then cool and chop. Fold into 300g sour cream with salt and chopped chives. Serve with a big bag of thick-cut potato chips.

s.note: Pretzel rods dipped in peanut butter, then milk chocolate
s.how: Warm 100g peanut butter with 1 tbsp honey and dip 20 pretzel rods halfway, then chill 15 minutes. Dip again in 150g melted milk chocolate and set on baking paper.

m.note: Breaded minute steak shallow fried, with peppery cream gravy
m.how: Pound 4 thin beef minute steaks. Dip in seasoned flour, then 2 beaten eggs, then flour again. Shallow fry in 1cm oil for 3 minutes a side. For the gravy, cook 2 tbsp flour in 2 tbsp of the oil, whisk in 500ml milk, simmer until thick and season with lots of black pepper.
